stories.headline: WHO pandemic hub aims to detect new outbreaks within 24 hours by 2030
stories.title: WHO pandemic hub aims to detect new outbreaks within 24 hours by 2030
stories.summary: WHO's pandemic hub aims to detect health threats within 24 hours by 2030, leveraging AI, pathogen surveillance, and global collaboration to enhance outbreak response and prevent crises.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: WHO has launched a five-year strategy for its pandemic intelligence hub, aiming to help every country detect emerging health threats within 24 hours by 2030.
The Berlin-based hub was created in 2021 after Covid-19 exposed gaps in global outbreak detection and response.
WHO says the hub has worked with 160 member states, 190 partner organisations and thousands of scientists and policymakers.
Its work will focus on open-source epidemic intelligence, pathogen surveillance, data science, collaborative surveillance and secure digital systems for public health intelligence.

The World Health Organization (WHO) has launched a five-year strategy for its pandemic intelligence hub, aiming to help every country detect and understand emerging health threats within 24 hours of their appearance by 2030.
The strategy for the WHO Hub for Pandemic and Epidemic Intelligence was announced at the opening of the World Health Summit in Berlin on October 12, 2026.
The WHO said faster detection was central to global health security, helping countries contain outbreaks before they escalate into larger epidemics or spread internationally.
The hub, based in Berlin, was created in 2021 with support from the German government after the Covid-19 pandemic exposed gaps in how countries detect and respond to emerging health threats.
WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the hub had become “an integral part of the global health security system” five years after its creation.

“Its new strategy charts a clear path towards 2030, uniting governments and partners around a shared goal: a world in which every country can rapidly respond to health threats before they turn into major crises,” he said.
The WHO said the hub has worked with 160 member states, 190 partner organisations and thousands of scientists and policymakers.
Its work includes detecting epidemic threats, sequencing and identifying pathogens, and supporting rapid action to protect communities.

stories.headline: Was Pinarayi ministry earnest about rebuilding Kerala after 2018 floods? CAG says no
stories.title: Was Pinarayi ministry earnest about rebuilding Kerala after 2018 floods? CAG says no
stories.summary: A CAG report exposed severe irregularities in Kerala's post-flood road reconstruction projects, including unauthorised sub-contracting, fraudulent completion bonuses, and major contractual deviations that benefited contractors at public expense.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: After the apocalyptic destruction unleashed by the 2018 floods, the Pinarayi Vijayan government projected the Rebuild Kerala Initiative (RKI) as the embodiment of Kerala's resilience.
RKI was supposed to be the dedicated agency to coordinate and implement recovery and reconstruction efforts.
Its mandate was to adopt world-class ecology-sensitive technology to insulate Kerala against future disasters.
But how shoddily and carelessly such a fight back was mounted is revealed in the report of the Comptroller and Auditor General that was tabled in the Assembly on Tuesday.
It was as if resilience was forgotten the moment the waters receded.
Under RKI, 29 PWD roads with a total length of 718.94 km across 13 districts were selected for reconstruction, with a sanctioned cost of ₹5119.54 crore.
The CAG put the microscope on 10 of these roads.

The audit noticed deficiencies in the preparation of detailed project reports, bidding documents and several instances of deviation from contractual provisions, all of which ended up causing project delays, recurring design changes and undue benefit to contractors.
Take, for instance, how irresponsibly, and in utter violation of the contract clause, work on the Uravanchal-Maruthayi stretch in North Kerala was carried out.
Clause 3.2.1 of the Engineering Procurement and Construction (EPC) contract prohibits sub-contracting beyond 25 per cent of the contract price.
Clause 3.2.2 mandates prior intimation to the Authority if any sub-contract exceeds five per cent of the contract price.
Unauthorised sub-contracting constitutes ‘Contractor Default’ under Clause 23.1.1(i), and Clause 23.1.2 empowers the Authority to terminate the contract with 15 days' notice.

stories.headline: Delhi High Court Directs Authorities To Provide Industrialist Anil Ambani's Son Details Of LOC Against Him
stories.title: Delhi High Court Directs Authorities To Provide Industrialist Anil Ambani's Son Details Of LOC Against Him
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Delhi High Court has directed the authorities to provide Jai Anshul Anil Ambani, son of industrialist Anil Ambani, specific details of the Look Out Circular (LOC) issued against him, including the date of its issuance, and a copy of the formal order.
Justice Mini Pushkarna passed the direction while hearing an application filed by Jai Anshul seeking compliance of an earlier order passed on September 17 by a coordinate bench.

The Court was informed that the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) had communicated to Jai Anshul on October 05 that an LOC had been issued against him in view of an ongoing investigation and that it continued to remain in force.
However, his counsel submitted that the communication was vague and did not disclose specific details regarding the LOC.
Taking note of the communication, the Court directed the authorities to provide details regarding when the LOC was issued and furnish a copy of the formal order to Jai Anshul in accordance with law.
The Court also took note of Ambani's submission that the communication was received only from the SFIO and not from the Bureau of Immigration.

“Accordingly, respondents are further directed to apprise the Court as to whether any other LOC has been issued against the petitioner, which is in the knowledge of the Bureau of Immigration,” the Court said.

During the hearing, counsel for the authorities submitted that the earlier direction had required the petition to be treated as a representation and requisite intimation to be provided within a time-bound manner.
It was argued that the Court had not directed the authorities to furnish specific details of the LOC.
The respondents also submitted that if Jai Anshul was dissatisfied with the communication issued by the SFIO, he could pursue other remedies available to him.
The matter will be considered next on October 16.

stories.headline: All about Gyanesh Kumar, the Chief Election Commissioner at the centre of the SIR row
stories.title: All about Gyanesh Kumar, the Chief Election Commissioner at the centre of the SIR row
stories.summary: Here’s a look at who Gyanesh Kumar is, what the objections are about, and where things currently stand.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Kumar, a 1988-batch IAS officer who took charge as CEC in February 2025, has defended the process as lawful and in line with Election Commission procedures.
The Election Commission has said internal differences among commissioners are part of normal institutional deliberation.
Here’s a look at who Gyanesh Kumar is, what the objections are about, and where things currently stand.
Why Gyanesh Kumar is at the centre of SIR controversy?
In late September 2026, Indian Express reported on the differences between the three-member Election Commission, placing Gyanesh Kumar's leadership under scrutiny.
Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi reportedly objected on record around 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders they said were taken without their knowledge.
Their objections reportedly concerned the SIR of electoral rolls, changes to voter registration Form 6, and the handling and control of electoral roll data.
Opposition parties, including the Congress, have alleged that eligible voters are being excluded and the process favoured the ruling BJP.
Not only did the poll body deny these allegations, Kumar also challenged Rahul Gandhi to substantiate his allegations of vote theft or apologise.
After criticism over the deletion of around 13 crore voters, the ECI ordered a special enrolment drive for voters left out during the SIR process.
Born in 1964, he received his schooling in Gorakhpur, Lucknow and Kanpur.
He topped the UP Board exams in high school in 1979 and intermediate in 1981.

stories.headline: Can CEC and Election Commissioners be prosecuted? Supreme Court examines legal immunity
stories.title: Can CEC and Election Commissioners be prosecuted? Supreme Court examines legal immunity
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court will examine a challenge to the legal immunity granted to the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners under the 2023 law.
The case raises questions about whether the protection of election officials from civil and criminal proceedings is consistent with constitutional accountability.

New Delhi: The Supreme Court has issued notice to the Centre and the Election Commission of India (ECI) on a petition filed by the Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) challenging the legal immunity granted to the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners for acts performed in the discharge of their official duties.

The challenge targets Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, which bars courts from entertaining or continuing civil or criminal proceedings against serving or former election commissioners for acts or statements made in the discharge, or purported discharge, of their official functions.
The petition has been tagged with related matters pending before the court and is scheduled to be heard alongside them on October 29.
The Supreme Court's latest notice brings the statutory protection available to India's top election officials under judicial scrutiny.

The petition, filed by ADR, challenges Section 16 of the 2023 Act, which provides immunity from civil and criminal proceedings for acts, things or words committed, done or spoken by a serving or former Chief Election Commissioner or Election Commissioner in the discharge, or purported discharge, of official duties.
The court has sought responses from the Union government and the Election Commission.
Issuing notice means the respondents have been asked to present their position; it does not mean the court has held the provision unconstitutional.

The case raises a fundamental legal question: how far can Parliament protect election commissioners from litigation arising out of their official functions without undermining the constitutional principles of accountability and the rule of law?
The provision does not, by its wording, extend to every act an election commissioner might commit in a personal capacity.
Its stated scope concerns conduct connected with the discharge, or purported discharge, of official duties.

stories.headline: SC issues notice to Centre, ECI on plea challenging blanket immunity to CEC, ECs
stories.title: SC issues notice to Centre, ECI on plea challenging blanket immunity to CEC, ECs
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday issued notice to the Centre and the Election Commission of India (ECI) on a public interest litigation challenging the blanket immunity granted to the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and other Election Commissioners under Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and the other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The plea seeks revival of proceedings against current and past CEC/Election Commissioners.

The Supreme Court today issued notice on a petition filed by the Association for Democratic Reforms challenging the immunity granted to Chief Election Commissioner/Election Commissioners for actions taken in purported discharge of official duties.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana sought the response of the Union and the Election Commission on ADR's challenge to the constitutional validity of Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.
Senior Advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan appeared for ADR.
The petition has been filed through AoR Rani Mishra.
Briefly put, the petition seeks a declaration that Section 16 of the CEC Act is unconstitutional, void and inoperative as violative of Articles 14 and 21 and the basic structure of the Constitution.
It further seeks revival of proceedings against the present and past CEC and Election Commissioners, which came to an end as Section 16 of the CEC Act came into effect.

"Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, no Court shall entertain or continue any civil or criminal proceedings against any person who is or was a Chief Election Commissioner or an Election Commissioner for any act, thing or word, committed, done or spoken by him when, or in the course of acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty or function."
The petition contends that Section 16 provides blanket immunity to the current and previous CEC/ECs for lifetime, which has no rational nexus with the objective of ensuring independence of CEC/ECs.
The provision places the CEC & ECs beyond the reach of any Court of law, it highlights.
"No other provision in the Constitution of India or any statute grants immunity that is at once lifelong, unconditioned by good faith, free of any sanction mechanism, and without a saving clause."
Petitioner-ADR further points out that Section 16 was not originally part of the Bill introduced.

stories.headline: RBI may raise repo rate by 75 bps, maintain tight stance through H1FY28
stories.title: RBI may raise repo rate by 75 bps, maintain tight stance through H1FY28
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 13 : The Reserve Bank of India is likely to stay on tightening path through H1FY28 and may hike the repo rate by around 75 basis points, according to leading brokerages. According to the NDTV Profit report, global brokerages -- including BofA, Goldman Sachs and UBS -- said that the Middle East tensions, energy supply disruptions and intensifying El Nino could push headline CPI higher. BofA and UBS have forecast that the central bank will tighten monetary policy and expect around a 75-basis-point repo rate hike in MPC meetings scheduled for FY27, extending up to the first half of fiscal 2028. Apart from that, UBS predicted full-year headline inflation to average near 5.2 per cent in FY27, while it could cross 5 per cent through first half of FY28 due to adverse weather-related strains. "As per our global strategy team, historical evidence suggests that effects typically materialize with a lag of 6-18 months following peak weather disruption. With likely peak occurring between November and February, most significant impact on global food prices may emerge during 2027 and early 2028, adding upside risks to inflation outlook," the brokerage forecasted. Additionally, they flagged upside risks after India's consumer inflation touched a 23-month high in September on surge in food prices. The report highlighted that headline Consumer Price Index inflation came at 5.54 per cent in September, up from 4.8 per cent in August, driven largely by higher food and vegetable prices. Moreover, food inflation climbed to 7.74 per cent in September from 5.97 per cent in August, while food and beverages inflation rose to 7.36 per cent from 5.66 per cent. Notably, rise in inflation was more pronounced in rural areas, where consumer inflation stood at 6.08 per cent in September, compared with 4.88 per cent in urban areas. CPI (General) index for combined category increased to 109.49 in September from 108.74 in August. Similarly, combined CFPI index rose to 112.17 from 110.73 during same period. --IANS

stories.headline: Punjab CM Beant Singh Assassination | Supreme Court Seeks Intelligence Bureau Inputs On Convict's Prison Transfer Plea
stories.title: Punjab CM Beant Singh Assassination | Supreme Court Seeks Intelligence Bureau Inputs On Convict's Prison Transfer Plea
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Tuesday sought inputs from the Intelligence Bureau (IB) on whether Jagtar Singh Hawara, convicted in the 1995 assassination of former Punjab Chief Minister Beant Singh, can be transferred from Tihar Jail in Delhi to a prison in Punjab, after concerns raised by the Punjab government over the possible impact on law and order.

A bench of Justice MM Sundresh and Justice PB Varale was hearing Hawara's plea seeking transfer to a jail in Punjab, primarily to enable him to meet his elderly mother, who is stated to be in serious condition.
The Court said that it would consider the request after obtaining the IB's assessment of the potential security and law-and-order implications of the transfer.
The Court observed that it could not disregard the Punjab government's objections, particularly since the case involved concerns that went beyond the individual prisoner.
It said that while it was inclined to consider such requests sympathetically, it had to ensure that its order did not trigger further problems in the state.
Justice Sundresh observed that the case could not be treated as an ordinary murder case because the state had raised concerns about the continuing influence of the ideology associated with the crime.
“But how do we ignore the objection of the Punjab state?...
The larger problem is still alive.
It is not that he has got a grievance.
It's not a simple case of 302.
That A killing B, B killing C, no problem, because it goes along with the person.
But it is based upon certain ideologies, certain views.

stories.title: Supreme Court stays defamation proceedings against Rahul Gandhi over 2018 remarks against PM Modi
stories.summary: The Opposition leader had challenged a Mumbai magistrate’s order to initiate proceedings against him on a complaint that his remarks had ‘hurt the sentiments of PM Modi’s supporters’
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) stayed criminal defamation proceedings against the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, over his alleged 2018 remarks calling Prime Minister Narendra Modi “commander-in-chief” over the Rafale fighter jet deal.

A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh passed the interim order on a petition filed by Mr. Gandhi challenging the Bombay High Court’s September 8 decision refusing to quash the proceedings.
“In the meantime, further proceedings before the trial court shall remain stayed,” the court ordered.
Senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, appearing for Mr. Gandhi, sought a stay on the ground that the proceedings were not maintainable.
The Bench also issued notice to the Maharashtra government and the complainant, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) member Mahesh Shrishrimal, and posted the matter for hearing after four weeks.
The complaint arose from two sets of remarks allegedly made by Mr. Gandhi in September 2018.

Mr. Shrishrimal objected to his use of the phrase “Hindustan ka chowkidar chor hai” at a rally in Rajasthan on September 20, 2018, and to a subsequent social media post in which he allegedly described the Prime Minister as “Commander in Thief”.

Mr. Shrishrimal alleged that the remarks imputed theft not only to Mr. Modi but also to members of the BJP and others associated with him, and sought Mr. Gandhi’s prosecution for criminal defamation under Section 500 of the Indian Penal Code.
Proceedings were initiated by a Mumbai Magistrate Court in 2019.
Mr. Gandhi subsequently moved the Bombay High Court in November 2021, denying the allegations and seeking quashing of the proceedings.
Justice N.R. Borkar of the High Court rejected Mr. Gandhi’s contention that the BJP was not an identifiable body for the purpose of the defamation complaint.

“On a prima facie reading of the defamatory statement, inter alia, it describes the Prime Minister, who is also the prominent face of the said political party, as having engaged in the acts of theft, while being the Commander of Thieves.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Refuses Plea Alleging Illegal House Entry By UP ATS, Asks Petitioner To Approach HC First
stories.title: Supreme Court Refuses Plea Alleging Illegal House Entry By UP ATS, Asks Petitioner To Approach HC First
stories.summary: The bench observed that the Court of first instance should be approached against alleged violation of fundamental rights.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The bench observed that the Court of first instance should be approached against alleged violation of fundamental rights.

The Supreme Court today refused to entertain a petition filed under Article 32 alleging that Uttar Pradesh ATS personnel entered the petitioner's house without proper uniform and identification even though there were no criminal proceedings pending against him.
The Court noted that the petitioner had not approached the Allahabad High Court at first instance and gave him liberty to avail that remedy.
A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana heard the matter.
During the hearing, considering the bench's disinclination, the petitioner's counsel questioned why the Supreme Court could not entertain an Article 32 petition claiming breach of fundamental rights.
The bench noted that the petitioner had not approached the High Court and had directly come to the Supreme Court.
"If I am coming under Article 32, the Supreme Court can't [shy away]", the petitioner's counsel responded.
At this point, Justice Bagchi opined that in Articles 32 and 226, there is an overlap qua the jurisdiction over breach of fundamental rights.
The judge said, "we would always [prefer] court of first instance to take cognizance of violation of fundamental rights."
The counsel contended, "it's guaranteed that Supreme Court cannot suspend fundamental rights".
Justice Bagchi replied, "you're right, but so can't High Court".
When the counsel persisted that the Parliament provided the jurisdiction to both the High Courts and the Supreme Court, Justice Bagchi said, "you have a fundamental duty to enforce those rights".

stories.headline: SC questions Delhi Police over alleged assault on women journalists
stories.title: SC questions Delhi Police over alleged assault on women journalists
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 13 : The Supreme Court on Tuesday took serious note of allegations that women journalists covering protests in the national capital were assaulted by police personnel and directed a senior Delhi Police officer to remain present during the hearing on Thursday to explain the matter. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana made the observation after senior advocate Indira Jaising mentioned a petition filed by the Network of Women in Media, India (NWMI), seeking safeguards for journalists covering protests, particularly women journalists. "We would like some senior officer to remain present here and explain," the CJI Kant-led Bench said, indicating that the police would have to explain the allegations. The development comes amid allegations that journalists covering protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar were manhandled, detained and obstructed while discharging their professional duties on October 10 and 11. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan also mentioned a separate contempt petition alleging that the police had assaulted journalists in violation of the Supreme Court’s October 10 order. The apex court had directed the authorities to ensure that lawyers, journalists and other professionals were not hindered in discharging their professional duties. The directions were passed by a Bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana while hearing contempt petitions alleging violations of its order concerning restrictions imposed ahead of the proposed protest. It had also directed the authorities to ensure the normal functioning of Metro and railway services, uninterrupted internet connectivity and free movement of people, subject to traffic regulations and public order requirements. The Supreme Court had also directed that there should be no detention except in accordance with the procedure established by law, particularly in the case of peaceful and unarmed gatherings outside areas where prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were in force. --IANS

stories.headline: BJP leader Kirit Somaiya seeks travel curbs on actor Imran Khan
stories.title: BJP leader Kirit Somaiya seeks travel curbs on actor Imran Khan
stories.summary: Mumbai, Oct 13 : BJP leader and former MP Kirit Somaiya has approached the Union Ministry of Home Affairs and immigration authorities, urging them to issue a Look Out Circular (LOC) against actor Imran Khan. He has also requested that the actor be barred from leaving the country until an inquiry into his complaint and the investigation into a Mumbai police case are completed. In a letter dated October 13 to Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Somaiya called on the Ministry of Home Affairs to issue directions preventing Khan from travelling abroad under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025. He also asked the Bureau of Immigration to issue an LOC against the actor and notify the police should he attempt to leave India. The move comes after a protest at Mumbai’s August Kranti Maidan on October 10 where demonstrators demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. In his letter, Somaiya claimed that the gathering had taken place without the necessary permission. He further alleged that Khan had attended and participated in the protest before Mumbai Police detained him at the venue. According to the letter, Gamdevi Police Station registered an FIR, numbered 813 of 2026, in connection with the incident, with Khan named in the case. Somaiya also stated that he had not received a copy of the FIR. Somaiya claimed in his letter that Khan is a US citizen and reportedly holds an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card. He urged the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Bureau of Immigration to assess whether the actor’s participation in the protest calls for action under Section 7D of the Citizenship Act, 1955, and the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025. Somaiya also took to X to share a copy of the letter addressed to the Union Home Secretary, detailing his request for a Look Out Circular against actor Imran Khan. Sharing the same, he wrote, “Requested Immigration Home Ministry to issue a LOC ( look out circular) against #ImranKhan to NOT to leave India.” Somaiya has further urged the Bureau of Immigration to alert Gamdevi Police Station if Khan attempts to travel outside India. He has also sought a written update from the concerned authorities on the steps taken in response to his request. Actor Imran Khan was detained by Mumbai Police on October 10 while attending a demonstration at August Kranti Maidan. He had joined a protest organized by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), which called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. --IANS

stories.headline: IMD: Heavy rain in Keralam, South Karnataka, TN, Puducherry for 4 days from Thursday
stories.title: IMD: Heavy rain in Keralam, South Karnataka, TN, Puducherry for 4 days from Thursday
stories.summary: Watch for low-pressure system over south-east Bay of Bengal withdrawn after parent circulation disappears, but South Peninsula is entering a consequential wet phase in seasonal calendar
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The South Peninsula is bracing for the arrival of the north-east monsoon, with the seasonal reversal of winds expected to gather momentum alongside the retreat of the south-west monsoon.

The trigger could be a low-pressure area forecast to develop over the south-east Bay of Bengal anytime now, setting the stage for the easterly flows that herald the onset of the second rainy season for the water-starved region.
The atmospheric signals are falling into place, with an upper-air cyclonic circulation over the South Andaman Sea poised to descend to lower levels and consolidate into the crucial low-pressure area.
At the western end of the Bay, another cyclonic circulation over the Gulf of Mannar could help draw in and channel the easterly winds, carrying the north-east monsoon deeper into the South Peninsula.
With the Bay of Bengal primed for a fresh low-pressure system and the retreating monsoon nearing its final exit, the South Peninsula is entering a consequential phase of the seasonal calendar.

The coming days will determine how quickly the easterlies take charge, and whether the expected onset of north-east monsoon brings a sustained spell of rain to the region after the south-west monsoon’s long retreat.
The emerging weather pattern is already offering a foretaste of the transition, with rain, thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds unfolding over several parts of southern India.
These conditions could intensify on either side of October 15, around which the north-east monsoon is likely to set in over Tamil Nadu and adjoining areas.
Its formal arrival could be announced during this phase.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD), in its Tuesday morning assessment, said conditions were becoming favourable for the south-west monsoon to withdraw from the remaining parts of the country and for north-east monsoon rains to commence over the South Peninsula simultaneously during the next 2-3 days.
The withdrawal line of the four-month south-west monsoon, which officially ended on September 30, continues to pass through Kolkata, Angul, Khammam and Honavar.
The predecessor monsoon must complete its retreat from the mainland before the seasonal transition is fully established, although the two processes can overlap in time.

stories.headline: ‘In a world where tariffs are a weapon…’: Uday Kotak says India must keep options open, look towards China
stories.title: ‘In a world where tariffs are a weapon…’: Uday Kotak says India must keep options open, look towards China
stories.summary: Uday Kotak said India must keep all its options open considering the changing economic nature of the ties with the US and Western countries.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Uday Kotak, Founder & Director, Kotak Mahindra Bank, said India must keep its options open and if it can’t beat China, then it must join them.
He said that India can’t really depend on the US now and must find takers in China.
Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum 2026 in New Delhi, Kotak said that in a world where tariffs are a weapon, strategic Chinese firms may be more open to investing in India.
"I think in a world where tariffs are a weapon, Chinese strategics may be more open to actually coming and investing in local domestic situations," Kotak said.

"If there are joint ventures between Chinese and Indian companies for manufacturing in India, the game China played with the US many years ago, that could be a path forward for India, and India has to keep its optionality open," he said.

"I think for India, if you can't beat them, join them, and we need to be open,” he said, adding that there are early signs that Indian companies are partnering with Chinese companies for Make in India and Chinese companies are welcome in India too.
He questioned India’s historical reliance on Western investments, and said it is necessary to explore alternative sources of capital, considering the evolving economic ties, especially with the US.

"Historically, India has looked too much to the West for investment, but with the challenges, particularly from the United States, and an overall more transactional approach to investment, the time has come for India to keep all its options open," he said.
